title: kv-tier-management
summary: Manage runtime KV cache tiers (GPU → CPU RAM → local disk) for LLM serving: decide when KV is stored, retained, prefetched, or evicted; size the concurrency-versus-RAM-pressure trade-off with an explicit in-flight admission dial; order RAM-release levers; and measure with token-level L1/L2 hit rates and prefetch-pressure counters. Use when configuring KV offload for a serving stack. Covers runtime KV offload only — model startup/loading, checkpoint save/restore, and block-device profiling are separate concerns (see weight-loading-optimization).

applicability.scope: LMCache multiprocess runtime KV tier policy across engine GPU cache, host L1 and configured L2 adapters, covering store/retention, prefetch admission, eviction and RAM pressure; startup loading and checkpoint recovery have separate owners.
applicability.prerequisites: The deployment uses the inspected MP-mode semantics rather than single-process knobs; selected GDS/DAX/raw-block paths need their own platform and adapter prerequisites. Lazy offload additionally requires vLLM prefix caching.
applicability.input_contract: MP versus single-process mode, store/retention policy and rationale, L1 manager capacities and eviction settings, L2 adapter capacities/eviction, chunk-size distribution and prefetch in-flight setting, together with token-level hit and pressure counters.
applicability.produced_artifact: A mode- and adapter-specific tier-policy choice with retention rationale, an ordered RAM-release plan and a verification record separating L1/L2 token hits, prefetch pressure, store lag and per-manager usage.
applicability.failure_modes: Mixing MP and in-process controls, treating key-count eviction as a byte fraction for unequal chunks, omitting fs capacity management, or increasing count-based prefetch admission without tracking L1 pressure can make the policy or memory claim unusable.

recommendations: Choose store retention and prefetched-key retention separately; use skip_l1 with noop only for buffer-only operation and account for failed stores remaining in L1.
Tune the count-based prefetch in-flight limit against L1 allocation failures and in-flight bytes; eager or warm prefetch can raise pressure before useful reuse.
Record per-adapter capacity/eviction and actual chunk-size uniformity; report token-level L1/L2 hits and sum per-l1_tag bytes rather than ratios.
